samples.summary: New exported `decimalsInValue` has no direct unit test; its documented text behaviour is unexercised (and looks false)
samples.evidence: `decimalsInValue` is a new exported function whose doc claims it returns `0` for "text", but `'a.bc'` would return 2. `packages/sheets/test/model/format.test.ts` contains no reference to it (grep for `decimalsInValue` matches only src files and no test), and `decimals.test.ts` only ever stores numeric values ('12', '12.5', '1234.5', '0.25', ...). The function is reached unconditionally from `getActiveDecimalState` (`decimalsInValue(cell?.v)`), i.e. for text cells too, so the untested branch is live.

samples.summary: The range-style-patch ownership branch of `unsetRangeStyleValues` (containsRange / rangesIntersect) is untested
samples.evidence: The sheet/column/row inheritance layers each get a dedicated test ('write an explicit value when a column/row/sheet style sets decimals', 'refuse a column unset when another column disagrees'), but nothing exercises a `rangeStyles` patch that intersects the selection without being contained by it — i.e. `owned(patch.range) === false` at sheet.ts:4395, the branch that prevents flattening a larger user patch. Every `setRangeStyle` call in decimals.test.ts is issued with either a single-cell selection (lines 118, 133, 226, 436) or a full column/row/sheet selection (296, 363, 381, 398-400); the only multi-cell patch test (line 185) re-selects exactly the same range, so `containsRange` always succeeds. A regression that let a partially overlapping patch be rewritten would silently pass this suite.
searchedFor: Read decimals.test.ts fully, inspected every setRangeStyle/selection combination
Grep for containsRange/rangesIntersect usages in tests

samples.summary: `selectionRendersAt`'s non-numeric skip branch is never exercised
samples.evidence: `selectionRendersAt` explicitly skips text/empty values (`if (!value || isNaN(Number(value))) continue;`), and that decision gates whether Decrease is a silent no-op for the whole selection. No test in decimals.test.ts stores a text value anywhere: every `setData` writes a numeric string. So a change that made text count as 'disagreeing' (turning a no-op Decrease into a style write across a text selection) would not be caught.
searchedFor: Grep changeDecimals call sites in tests

samples.summary: Grouping/format expectations are computed with `formatValue` and depend on the ambient system locale, so they do not pin the behaviour the test names claim
samples.evidence: Tests at lines 31-33, 109-111, 155-157, 238-240, 445-447 and 478-483 assert `toDisplayString(...)` equals `formatValue(<same value>, 'number', <dp>)`. `formatValue` resolves the locale via `resolveSystemLocale()` (format.ts:120, locale.ts:142), which reads the ambient environment; no test pins a locale. The test titled 'should keep the grouping separators the step would flatten' never asserts that a separator is present ('1,234.5'), only that two calls to the same formatter agree — under a locale without grouping the intended distinction disappears while the assertion text still reads as coverage of grouping. The strong assertion in that test is the preceding `toEqual({dp: 1, nf: 'number'})`; the display assertion adds little and is locale-fragile.
searchedFor: Glob for packages/sheets vitest config to check locale/TZ pinning (none found)

samples.summary: No test covers the view-level `increaseDecimals`/`decreaseDecimals` rewiring or its read-only guard
samples.evidence: `Spreadsheet.increaseDecimals`/`decreaseDecimals` were rewritten to delegate to `sheet.changeDecimals(±1)` and still carry the `_readOnly` early return, but grep for `increaseDecimals|decreaseDecimals` finds hits only in spreadsheet.ts and packages/frontend/src/components/formatting-toolbar.tsx — no test file. A delegation with the wrong sign, or a lost read-only guard, would not be caught by any suite. (Pre-existing gap, but the call sites changed in this diff.)

samples.summary: The merged-cell anchor normalization/dedupe in `unsetRangeStyleValues` is untested
samples.evidence: `unsetRangeStyleValues` normalizes each grid ref to its merge anchor and dedupes via a `visited` set (sheet.ts:4407-4412). No decimals test creates a merged region (no `merge` call anywhere in decimals.test.ts), so double-visiting or wrong-anchor writes on merged cells — the reason that code exists — has no coverage. merge behaviour is tested elsewhere (test/sheet/merge.test.ts) but not in combination with the new unset path.

samples.summary: `omitStyleKeys` and the empty-request/no-op returns of `unsetRangeStyleValues` have no direct tests
samples.evidence: `omitStyleKeys` is a new export in range-styles.ts; packages/sheets/test/model/range-styles.test.ts contains no reference to it (grep for `omitStyleKeys|mergeStylePatch` in that file returned no matches), so its documented 'returns undefined when the style carries none of the keys' contract is only covered incidentally. Likewise `unsetRangeStyleValues({})` → false (sheet.ts:4338) and the 'nothing turned out to be removable' → false return are documented public behaviours with no test.

finding.summary: compactCell's new spill-field preservation ships with no test
finding.evidence: The diff adds four new branches to `compactCell` copying `spillRows`, `spillCols`, `spillAnchor`, `spillBlocked` from the base cell, justified by a comment that "a style-only rewrite must not detach a dynamic-array anchor from its ghosts". Nothing in the suite exercises that: `grep -rn 'spill' packages/sheets/test` matches only calculation.test.ts, data-validation.test.ts and formula.test.ts, and `grep -n 'setStyle|setRangeStyle|clearFormat' packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts` returns no matches — the spill tests never mutate styles, and formatting.test.ts never creates a spill. The new decimals.test.ts never sets a spilling formula either. So the regression this hunk fixes (style write on a spill anchor dropping the spill metadata, reachable via sheet.ts:3682 setStyle, sheet.ts:2007 clearCellStylesInRange and the new sheet.ts:4447 unset path) can break again with the suite fully green.

verdict.reason: A dedicated test file for this exact hunk exists at packages/sheets/test/model/style-mutation.test.ts, contradicting the finding's cited grep. My own grep for 'spill' under packages/sheets/test returns 16 hits in that file — the reviewer's claim that only calculation/data-validation/formula match is factually wrong (they likely searched a stale tree or missed the test/model subdirectory). Coverage is at two levels. (1) Unit: lines 13-34 call compactCell directly and deep-equal assert all four new branches — spillRows/spillCols on an anchor (18-24), spillAnchor on a ghost (26-27), spillBlocked (29-33); deleting any new branch makes the toEqual fail, so the assertions are not vacuous. (2) Integration: lines 37-74 build a real Sheet over a real MemStore (39-40, nothing mocked), create a genuine spill with =MMULT(A1:B2,C1:D2), snapshot spillRows/spillCols/spillAnchor (51-55), perform the style-only write via sheet.setStyle (58-59) — which routes through compactCell at sheet.ts:3682, the exact regression path the finding names — and re-assert the metadata survived (61-67). The test also guards against being fake coverage: lines 70-73 overwrite the anchor with =SUM(A1:B2) and assert the ghost renders '', proving the preserved metadata is live rather than inert data copied along; line 68 confirms the ghost still displays '22'. The file is collected by the runner: packages/sheets/vite.config.ts declares no custom include, so vitest's default **/*.test.ts glob picks it up. The only residual gap is that the integration test drives setStyle but not clearCellStylesInRange (sheet.ts:2007) or the unset path (sheet.ts:4492) — under this lens's rubric that is at most a minor breadth point, not the asserted "ships with no test".
